text:
maya: Heads up — npm package 'redwood-utils' v1.3.2 was published this morning and the README contains a raw internal service API key (looks like rw_svc_abc123...). npm-scan flagged it. Can security help triage?

sam: which key type is that? ingest / customer-facing / deployment?

maya: pattern match shows it's our telemetry ingest service key (svc.ingest). Prefix rw_svc_. Not a user API key. Not sure how it ended up in README — likely copy/paste from local dev.

security-bot: Alert: npm-scan detected exposed secret in package redwood-utils@1.3.2 README. Link: https://npm-scan.internal/redwood-utils/1.3.2

jonathan: Revoke immediately if we can. Also we need to assess scope (was the key used) and whether any customer data was touched. sam, can you take revocation?

sam: On it. Steps I'll run: 1) revoke key in KMS/service control plane, 2) create rotated key, 3) update CI envs + redeploy telemetry client. Anyone have quick grep queries for usage now?

maya: Quick log query we used: 
```
# datadog/elk query
service:telemetry AND api_key:"rw_svc_abc123*" AND @timestamp:[now-24h TO now]
```
That showed ~120 hits in the last 6 hours from a mix of staging and a couple of prod host IPs.

lucy: Do customers show up in those requests? any PII?

maya: Early check: payloads for those ingestion events look like anonymized metrics (counts, uptime). No obvious customer payloads found in body samples but we need a fuller search.

sam: I'm going to revoke now. Will rotate and post updates. If we revoke, we should also add a short-lived fallback key and set a short canary window to avoid ingestion gaps. jonathan, can infra do a quick canary rollout?

jonathan: Yes. We'll push new key to CI as RW_TELEMETRY_KEY_NEW and set routing: 90% new / 10% old for 10 minutes then cutover. Also add rate-limit guard as contingency.

maya: Also we should contact npm support and request takedown or at least remove the README content. We can deprecate the package version and publish a fixed 1.3.3.

sam: Commands I'll run: 
```
npm deprecate redwood-utils@1.3.2 "exposed secret - use 1.3.3"
# publish patched version
npm publish ./packages/redwood-utils --tag latest
```
Note: npm unpublish may be restricted; we'll request abuse support if needed.

security-bot: Reminder: create an incident ticket and link PRs + timelines.

maya: I've kicked off a full search for the string across our repos and artifacts: 
```
# repo/file scan (running)
rg "rw_svc_abc123" --hidden --no-ignore -S || true
```
If it appears elsewhere we escalate rotation.

lucy: Any customer comms required? If telemetry ingestion was only metrics and anonymized, maybe not, but legal should confirm. I'll loop legal/compliance.

sam: Revocation update: rw_svc_abc123 revoked at 2223456800 UTC. New key issued (rw_svc_def456) and pushed to CI as part of hotfix pipeline. Canary in progress.

jonathan: Canary looks clean. 15m with 90% new key, 0 errors for telemetry. We cut 100% to new key at 2223456818.

maya: npm takedown request opened with support ticket #NPM-4982. We've deprecated 1.3.2 and published 1.3.3 with the README removed. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/987

sam: Post-incident actions we should capture: 1) update dev onboarding doc to ban pasting live keys in READMEs, 2) add pre-publish CI scan blocking rule for packages containing rw_svc_*, 3) rotate keys quarterly + automated alerting improvements, 4) legal to review customer comms threshold.

maya: I'll own the post-incident report and RCA. Will include timeline, root cause (dev copy/paste), detection (npm-scan), containment steps, and long-term remedial actions. Filing incident in pagerduty postmortem bucket.

lucy: Thanks all — cc @legal @compliance for signoff on customer messaging if needed.

ci-bot: Deploy logs: hotfix/redwood-utils published 1.3.3 by sam — build 4421 — all checks passed.

maya: Closing thread to follow up in the formal incident doc. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
